payload.goal: Hold the stated H2 direction — watcher, sync, faster indexing using AI, sofar serving each agent only the piece it needs, and model orchestration — against the record, so each thread is either pointed at its existing initiative or carries an explicit ruling. Opened as direction capture, not as work: no task is started from here until the one guard-rail conflict it contains is ruled on.

payload.text:
GUARD-RAIL CONFLICT, surfaced not ruled (CLAUDE.md requires logging the conflict and handing it to the user; no work started).

The five stated threads, held against the record:

1. WATCHER — already shipped. chokidar in the engine, `sofar serve`, plus the doorbell SSE client and `sofar pull --watch` from sync-client 3.3. Nothing new required; any H2 work here is extension.

2. SYNC — already shipped, and explicitly blessed. sync-client is 15/15 tasks done: login by RFC-8628 device flow, link, push/pull with offline queue, ack cursors and doorbell SSE. SPEC Architectural invariants names it as the SOLE permitted egress: "The ONLY egress in the product is the v2 sync client (sync-client D4)". Note the CLAUDE.md rail "DO NOT build the sync service/backend" bites the SERVER, not the client — the client is done and sanctioned. Do not re-litigate it as forbidden.

3. SOFAR SHARES THE REQUIRED PIECE TO AGENTS — this is the product thesis, not a new capability, and it already has an implementation: core/index-tier1.ts is exactly "declared relevance, keyed for lookup" so the guard, the session-start priming line and mid-task search can each get only their piece. Extension work is unblocked.

4. MODEL ORCHESTRATION — already in flight as session-driver, and already cleared. session-driver D1 ruled that launching the operator's OWN agent process under the operator's own auth is not a model call, because that process's inference is the operator's and sofar needs no key, no call and no egress to launch it. Proceed there, not here.

5. FASTER INDEXING USING AI — THE ONLY GENUINE COLLISION, and it is blocked twice over, so it cannot be waved through:
   (a) SPEC Architectural invariants: "sofar never calls a model: no API keys, no inference costs, no user content fed to any model... Any change that would add a model call to sofar (e.g. cheap-model or Batch-API bookkeeping) is rejected until a Decision explicitly revisits this invariant (felt-cost D3)."
   (b) More pointedly, the indexing layer ALREADY faced this exact temptation and refused it. SPEC pins record-graph citation extraction as "a CLOSED LEXICAL GRAMMAR with literal matching only — no inference, no embeddings, no entity resolution", alongside a determinism law: the same records must build a deep-equal graph. Embedding-based indexing breaks determinism as well as the zero-model rule, so replay would stop being reproducible.

   A WAY THROUGH THAT COSTS NO RULING, worth considering before spending the invariant: apply the D1 carve-out one layer up. The operator's agent is already running and already paid for, so let IT produce the enrichment — summaries, groupings, relevance hints — and emit them as ordinary events in packages/schema that sofar only stores, folds and serves. sofar still never calls a model, holds no key, and sends nothing anywhere; determinism survives because the fold is still a pure function of the event set. What is lost is that enrichment becomes non-retroactive, produced only for records an agent has actually visited. If the user wants the OTHER version — sofar embedding records itself — that needs a Decision explicitly superseding both SPEC Architectural invariants and felt-cost D3, logged BEFORE any work, per the session-driver D1 amendment to the rails.

RUNTIME CONSEQUENCE, relevant because this session just settled it: the Rust/Zig verdict rested on sofar being IO-bound. Vector or embedding indexing is CPU-bound, and it is the one item on this roadmap that could flip that finding. If 5 lands in its embedding form, the runtime question reopens on merit and the artifact at https://claude.ai/code/artifact/ff9f4ee7-ede7-4d11-be78-d47eba7f206a must be revisited rather than cited.

payload.next_action: Rule on item 5, faster indexing using AI, before any work starts on it: either take the agent-emitted enrichment route, which needs no Decision because sofar still never calls a model, or log a Decision explicitly superseding SPEC Architectural invariants and felt-cost D3 for the embedding route, before the work and never after, per the guard-rail amendment in session-driver D1. Items 1 through 4 need nothing from this initiative and should be pursued in their own records.
payload.summary: Opened roadmap-h2 as direction capture, not work, and held the five stated H2 threads against the record. Four need no ruling: the watcher already ships (chokidar, serve, and the doorbell SSE with pull watch from sync-client 3.3); sync already shipped as sync-client at 15 of 15 tasks and is named in SPEC Architectural invariants as the sole permitted egress, so the CLAUDE.md rail against the sync service bites the server and not the client; serving each agent only the piece it needs is the product thesis and already has core index-tier1 as its implementation; and model orchestration is in flight as session-driver with its path already cleared by D1. The fifth, faster indexing using AI, is the only genuine collision and it is blocked twice: SPEC Architectural invariants forbids sofar calling a model at all, and more pointedly the indexing layer already refused this exact temptation, since record-graph citation extraction is pinned as a closed lexical grammar with literal matching only, no inference, no embeddings, no entity resolution, alongside a determinism law that the same records build a deep-equal graph. Logged the conflict as a note per CLAUDE.md rather than ruling on it. Also proposed a way through that spends no invariant: apply the session-driver D1 carve-out one layer up, letting the operator's already-running agent emit enrichment as ordinary schema events that sofar only stores, folds and serves, which keeps sofar keyless and the fold deterministic at the cost of enrichment being non-retroactive. Flagged the runtime consequence: the Rust and Zig verdict reached earlier this session rests on sofar being IO-bound, and embedding-based indexing is CPU-bound, so it is the one roadmap item that would reopen that question on merit.
